semantically_equivalent_models.justification: "Optimal transport conditional flow matching" is a specialized type of flow matching model that deals with optimal transport in conditional settings, making it semantically equivalent to "flow matching models."

"Conditional flow matching" are a specific kind of flow matching model focusing on conditional distributions, which makes them semantically equivalent to the broader category of "flow matching models."

parent_models.justification: Normalizing flows are a more general category of deep learning models that include flow-based models, which encompass flow matching models. Flow matching models are a subset of normalizing flows, thus making them parent models.

closest_parent_model.justification: Among the parent models, "normalizing flows" is the broad category under which flow matching models fall directly. This makes it the closest parent model for flow matching models.

child_models.justification: As a specific application of flow matching models dealing with optimal transport, this model is more specialized and thus a child model of flow matching models.

closest_child_model.justification: "Conditional flow matching" directly describes a subcategory of flow matching models without any additional complexity, making it the closest child model compared to other variations like "optimal transport conditional flow matching."

sibling_models.justification: Normalizing flows are related but do not specialize in matching techniques, thereby serving as sibling models to flow matching under the broader category of flow-based models.

closest_sibling_model.justification: "Generative flow network" is closely related as it is also a type of flow-based model and often used in similar contexts to flow matching models, making it the closest sibling.
